provenance.source: SolidWorks battery_box.stl + battery_bracket.stl, exported in their OWN part frames, in MILLIMETRES
how_derived: The SolidWorks trunk aggregate puts the new battery assembly's CoM at (-31.1, ~0, -1.9) mm in the trunk body frame (solving M_new*C_new = m_rest*c_rest + m_bat*c_bat, assuming the rest of the link is unchanged).
Orienting the box's 88 mm axis along body +Z, its 43 mm axis along +Y, and the bracket's thin 9 mm axis along +X in front of it, the CoM constraint fixes the translation.
The resulting box spans x[-42.8,-23.5] y[+/-21.5] z[-45.8,+42.1] mm, i.e. it almost exactly fills the trunk envelope -- evidence the orientation is right, but NOT proof.
provenance.how_to_correct: Change pos_mm / quat_wxyz below (quat (0.5,0.5,0.5,0.5) means part X->body +Y, part Y->body +Z, part Z->body +X) and re-run scripts/apply_battery_geometry.py --write
history: battery_bracket pos_mm[0] -27.061 -> -21.061 on user request ('move it 6 mm forward'); the previous value was invented, not measured, so the bracket was sitting inside power_support and its bolt holes could not line up.
user tuned both parts by hand (box -4 mm X / -5 mm Z, bracket +2 mm X / -1 mm Z).

battery_box pos_mm[0] -50.34 -> -51.62 to make the box front face / bracket rear face gap exactly 6.00 mm (was 4.72). The BOX was moved rather than the bracket so the bracket's bolt-hole alignment is untouched; moving the bracket +1.28 mm instead would give the same 6.00 mm.

why: power_support IS the original battery bracket: a 17 x 54.5 x 83.5 mm vertical T-shaped plate, the same shape family as the new battery_bracket (9 x 54 x 72 mm) and the same 54 mm width.
The volume accounting confirms it: old power_support 10.5 cm3 -> new battery_bracket 5.6 cm3, and the trunk total went 118.9 -> 111.7 cm3.

It is class='self_collision_only' in all 8 models (contype=conaffinity=2), so it never touched the floor. Measured impact of deleting it: trunk self-collision count is IDENTICAL in every pose and every model (STAND/SIT/FOLD 0,0,0; allcollisions FOLD 8 before and after), so the self_collision sensor is unaffected too.
The <mesh file=.../> declaration and the geom/comment lines are removed; power_support.stl is left on disk as an archive of the old part.
